# Webhooks

Ferrowave sends events to your HTTPS endpoint. Every delivery is signed.

- [Verifying signatures](https://docs.ferrowave.dev/guides/webhooks/verify-signatures)
- [Retries](https://docs.ferrowave.dev/guides/webhooks/retries)

title: Verifying webhook signatures | Ferrowave Docs
content: Verify the Ferrowave-Signature-V2 header (HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp and body) on every webhook delivery.
raw_content:
# Verifying webhook signatures

Every webhook delivery carries a `Ferrowave-Signature-V2` header: `t=<unix timestamp>,v2=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">` signed with your endpoint secret.

Reject deliveries whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes old.

## Migrating from v1 signatures

The v1 `X-Ferrowave-Sig` header (HMAC-SHA1) is still sent alongside v2 for now. Ferrowave will **stop sending v1 webhook signatures on January 15, 2027**. Switch your verification to `Ferrowave-Signature-V2` before then.

title: Webhook retries | Ferrowave Docs
content: Failed webhook deliveries are retried with exponential backoff for up to 3 days.
raw_content:
# Webhook retries

# API keys

Use restricted keys (`fw_rk_...`) for server-side integrations.

> Legacy v1 API keys (`fw_live_...`) stop working on **December 1, 2026**. Rotate to v2 keys from the dashboard.

# Webhooks (v1, archived)

> Archived March 2025. This page is no longer maintained.

v1 webhook deliveries are signed with the `X-Ferrowave-Sig` header (HMAC-SHA1 of the body). v1 webhooks are supported until June 30, 2026.

title: Introducing signed webhooks v2 | Ferrowave Blog
content: Webhook signatures v2 use HMAC-SHA256 and include a timestamp to stop replay attacks. Migration details are in the docs.
raw_content:
# Introducing signed webhooks v2

Webhook signatures v2 use HMAC-SHA256 and include a timestamp to stop replay attacks. We expect to retire v1 signatures sometime in 2027; the docs have the exact date.
